rationale: Across the published literature describing Fliedner-Zweier syndrome (SCAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder), evaluated neuroimaging consistently demonstrates either completely normal intracranial anatomy or non-specific findings such as mild white matter anomalies and periventricular changes. Gross structural malformations (such as holoprosencephaly, lissencephaly, or severe posterior fossa malformations) have not been reported as a primary or recurrent manifestation, meaning gross structural malformations are absent in well over 70% of evaluated individuals.

evidence.text: Evaluated individuals with pathogenic SCAF4 variants presented with neurodevelopmental delay, seizures, and aspecific brain MRI findings rather than recurrent major structural malformations.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact percentage and granular breakdown of specific minor neuroimaging features (such as delayed myelination, thin corpus callosum, or ventricular asymmetry) across all pooled SCAF4 cases with neuroimaging available?
new_directions.rationale: While gross cortical malformations are absent, systematic documentation of minor neuroimaging features across large cohorts like the 50-patient Tran Mau series will help establish specific positive neuroimaging criteria.
